answer: In an agent market monitoring shale near a summit, each agent must lock tokens for 30 days to bid for work. The scheduler assigns jobs in proportion to locked stake, so splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities earns the same expected workload as one identity holding 100. Each sensor pulse can attract new bidders, but extra names create no extra share: an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens to capture more of the market.
